questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 23 \\ 23 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 23\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 27 \\ -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}17 & 23 \\ 23 & 85\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 23\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=17+85+13=115.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -16 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9\cdot 8-(-2)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{68}[\begin{aligned}68 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {3}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 18 \\ -8 & -16 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 \\ -16 \\ 36\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}25 & 50 \\ 50 & 100\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}50 \\ 100\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}25 & 50 & 50 \\ 50 & 100 & 100\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}25 & 50 & 50 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=2-2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=2+\frac{(-2)}{1}=0.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $17a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ -6 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ -6 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ -6 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 4 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ -6 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}17 & -34 \\ -34 & 68\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}17 & -34 & 3 \\ -34 & 68 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}17 & -34 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{3}{17}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{17}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{17} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
17a+\frac{b}{c}=17(\frac{3}{17})+\frac{2}{1}=5.
$$

$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -8 \\ -8 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {4}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 8 & 4 \\ -16 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}32 & -8 \\ -8 & 24\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=32+24+8=64.
$$
